findings.claim: GS4, Q1 and ADR-0003 make deleting v1 tests an exit criterion, with no gate that v1 tests of kept parts pass. Owner decision: v2 is built until v1 unit tests pass; at least the kept parts must pass.
findings.evidence: TECH-SPEC.md:37 'GS4 | v1 `tests/` is deleted'; :404 'Q1 Delete v1 tests in one commit once GS1 holds'; adr/0003:1 'unit tests are deleted'; :35. No criterion names v1 test pass status.
findings.fix: Add an exit criterion: v1 tests mapped to kept behaviour run against v2 and PASS; ledger verdict 'KEPT-PASS' per row. Retitle ADR-0003.

findings.claim: PRD still describes per-session DBs, sibling read-only DBs and 'doctor --fix' deletes one session DB. This conflicts with ADR-0002 single context.db, and the TECH-SPEC superseded table does not list these lines.
findings.evidence: PRD-v2.md:80-84 'No shared writable DB', 'open sibling DBs', 'Delete a session DB', '`--fix` deletes only that session DB'; PRD:146,161,173; adr/0002:17 one file per project; TECH-SPEC.md:52-58 omits these rows.
findings.fix: Add PRD §6 storage lines, E7, E19 and §146 to the TECH-SPEC superseded table with ADR-0002 as successor; define corruption handling for the single DB.

findings.claim: Tool count is 7 in README, PRD §7, TECH-SPEC §3.3 and GP1, but 9 in PRD addendum and §3.11 (ctx_doctor, ctx_upgrade kept as tools).
findings.evidence: TECH-SPEC.md:107 '(×7)'; :287 GP1 'tools/list (7 tools)'; README.md:101 '7 tools'; PRD-v2.md:289 '9 tools — ... ctx_doctor, ctx_upgrade, ctx_purge'; TECH-SPEC.md:213 'kept, rebuilt for v2'.
findings.fix: Pick one list (9) and update README:101, TECH-SPEC:107, GP1, §3.5 budgets and lint counts.

findings.claim: WebFetch deny names ctx_fetch_and_index, which v2 removes (absorbed into ctx_index). A deny would name a tool that does not exist: a dead end, the #794 class.
findings.evidence: adr/0008:10 'deny, same alternative' (ctx_fetch_and_index); :46 'names `ctx_fetch_and_index` with the URL'; PRD-v2.md:126 'ctx_index ... absorbs `ctx_fetch_and_index`'; README.md:101.
findings.fix: Name ctx_index with {url} then ctx_search; add a GP3 golden that every tool name in a deny exists in tools/list.

findings.claim: Case B adds two shipped executables (run.mjs, search.mjs) that the model runs via Bash. This is a CLI surface, against 'no CLI', and it is missing from the §4 layout and GP coverage.
findings.evidence: adr/0016:27 'node <bundle>/run.mjs <base64>' and 'more: node <bundle>/search.mjs'; README.md:25 'no CLI'; TECH-SPEC.md:4 layout has no run.mjs/search.mjs; PRD-v2.md:196 G12-G14 'no CLI'.
findings.fix: Record the exception as a decision (bundle-internal entries, not user CLI), add them to §4 and to GP4/GP5 cases, and pin their argv contract.

findings.claim: Subagent tool discovery (read .claude/agents/<type>.md, project then user dir, parse frontmatter) is Claude-Code-specific logic with a lookup order. ADR-0001 says adapters hold no routing logic; the doc does not say where this lives, nor what other agents do.
findings.evidence: adr/0016:19 'the server reads .claude/agents/<type>.md (project, then user dir)'; adr/0001:23 'It holds no prompt text, no routing logic and no state'; adr/0016:16 'the hook payload carries agent_type' (Claude Code only).
findings.fix: Put subagent-capability resolution in core with an adapter-supplied capability row; state the result for each of the 10 agents; say how a name collision between project and user dir resolves.

findings.claim: GS6 (hook p95 <= 40 ms for every adapter) cannot hold: ADR-0008 measured bare Node at 45.6 ms p95. ADR-0010 D5 and GP3 also assert 40 ms.
findings.evidence: TECH-SPEC.md:39 'GS6 | Hook wall time p95 <= 40 ms for every adapter'; adr/0008:71 'bare Node is 45.6 ms p95 ... cannot meet'; adr/0010:32 '<= 40 ms'.
findings.fix: Replace GS6, GP3 and D5 with one metric (e.g. CPU on top of bare Node) once the owner decides; keep the number in one place.

findings.claim: §3.8 lists two Claude Code tool names (plain MCP and plugin). PRD E14 says one install mode per agent. Which one the adapter row holds is not stated, so matchers may have to choose at run time.
findings.evidence: TECH-SPEC.md:185-186 two rows for Claude Code; PRD-v2.md:168 'E14 | One install mode per agent'; TECH-SPEC.md:202 'one install mode per agent'.
findings.fix: State the one Claude Code install mode (plugin) and drop the other row, or document it as a doctor error.

findings.claim: The single-DB table list (events, sources, chunks, meta) misses tables other ADRs add: hook_error_day, deny_day, and the readiness rows.
findings.evidence: README.md:79; adr/0014:48-49 'hook_error_day', 'deny_day'; adr/0008:27 'the server writes a `ready` row'.
findings.fix: Keep one schema list (ADR-0002) that names every table, and reference it from the other ADRs.

findings.claim: README says 'no skills' and TECH-SPEC lists ADRs 0001-0006 only; both are stale against decided §3.9 (3 skills) and ADR-0007..0016.
findings.evidence: README.md:25 'no CLI, no skills'; TECH-SPEC.md:205 'User commands as skills [D 2026-10-14]'; TECH-SPEC.md:4 'ADRs: 0001–0006'.
findings.fix: Update README principles to 'no routing skills; 3 command skills' and the TECH-SPEC header ADR range.

findings.claim: Owner rule: issue templates are fully for AI agents; an agent that reads them must follow our rules and send maximum debug data. bug.yml is written for a human (dropdown 'did doctor run?', free text) and gives an agent no step list.
findings.evidence: adr/0014:57 'Run `/ctx-doctor`, or tell the agent: call the ctx_doctor tool.' plus human dropdown/textarea; no agent-directed instructions, no required machine fields beyond the report; owner rule in this run's request.
findings.fix: Rewrite §5 so each form is an agent procedure: call ctx_doctor, paste the full report, add hook fixtures and deny journal rows, fill typed fields; state the rules the agent must follow; GP11 checks the form.
